assertion.quantifiers: Every false triple in the listed finite box and every true canonical triple tested by the guard.
assertion.parameter_range: Integer indices and rational point-code coordinates; the finite product uses exactly the prescribed false triples.
assertion.uniformity: The same fixed recipe and guard apply to every allowed input.
assertion.constants: The actual T and D_abc are fixed before testing inputs; no new cutoff estimate is supplied here.

assertion.statement: The two actual extra Kummer classes on E_n and E_(n theta), after restricted RC and forward analytic-rank-one imply Sha[2]=0, produce exactly eleven rational witnesses for the original pole template with the same B and m.
assertion.objects: Points(x1,y1),(x2,y2), x_i=A q_i^2, H=theta c^2, e=n/q1^2,z=c q2/q1,r1=y1/q1^3,r2=c^3 y2/(q1^3 z),w=(eHz)^(-1), and the six already chosen bits of m.
assertion.hypotheses: Both n,n theta are positive squarefree congruent11 mod12, with full2-Selmer dimension3, full2-infinity Selmer corank1 and extra class(beta,1) outside all rational2-torsion images. Retain restricted RC, rational modularity and the forward rank-one theorem.
assertion.quantifiers: For the original fixed B,m,A,H and the simultaneous pair n,n theta, choose rational representatives of their actual Kummer classes only after proving Sha[2]=0.
assertion.parameter_range: All q_i,c,e,z are nonzero rational numbers; theta=1 is allowed.
assertion.uniformity: Works for every B in the PC domain supplied by the simultaneous construction; no extra independent multiplier choice.
assertion.constants: Exactly the original six bits and five rational witnesses; no new template variables.
assertion.normalizations: Second point is(Az^2,z r2) on E_(eH). Dividing its cubic equation by z^2 yields r2^2=A(Az^2-eH)(Az^2+3eH), retaining leading factor A.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Extra class excludes infinity and all root points, so ordinates/abscissas and all denominators are nonzero. If theta=1 reuse one point and take q2=q1. Finite Sha is concluded from forward rank only, never assumed for RC.
assertion.limit_order: Exact Selmer dimension then full corank, then two restricted RC applications, then forward rank and Sha[2]=0, then actual points and final rational scaling.

assertion.statement: For the actual elliptic curve E/Q, the Cassels–Tate pairing induces a nondegenerate alternating pairing on the quotient of Sha(E) by its maximal divisible subgroup, hence on its finite2-primary quotient F in the supplied decomposition.
assertion.objects: The canonical principal polarization on E, Sha(E), its maximal divisible subgroup, and F=Sha(E)[2∞]/Sha(E)[2∞]_div.
assertion.hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve over Q. The supplied finite-Selmer/cofinite-generation input gives Sha(E)[2∞]=(Q2/Z2)^t⊕F with F finite. No finiteness of the full Sha group is assumed.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve E/Q; the finite-quotient application holds for its actual2-primary decomposition.
assertion.parameter_range: Canonical genus-one principal polarization;2-primary quotient by maximal divisibility, not the unrestricted pairing on2-torsion.
assertion.uniformity: No quantitative bound or uniform finiteness statement.
assertion.constants: The quotient has paired finite primary cyclic factors; in particular dim_F2 F[2] is even.
assertion.normalizations: Cor4 gives c via Pic^(g−1); at g=1 the trivial degree-zero class makes c=0. Cor7 gives alternation. Nondegeneracy is after maximal-divisible quotient. Different primary torsion components are orthogonal.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Do not equate infinitely divisible elements with the maximal divisible subgroup in an arbitrary group. Current decomposition proves maximality directly. Do not infer nondegeneracy of the restriction to F[2], or finiteSha, or Mordell–Weil rank1 before RC.
assertion.limit_order: First use the separately supplied decomposition and identify its maximal divisible subgroup. Then restrict the quotient pairing to the finite2-primary part and apply the paired-factor argument; only afterward combine with Kummer dimensions.

assertion.statement: For every B in the stated pole-completeness domain, one common positive signed divisor m of2730 gives A=mB,H=A(A-B^2), with positive squarefree classes beta congruent17 mod24 and theta congruent1 mod24. There exist positive squarefree n,n theta congruent11 mod12 for which the full multiplication-by-two Selmer groups have dimension3 and contain the same extra class(beta,1).
assertion.objects: The same B,m,A,H,beta,theta; support matrices K,s,lambda and the two actual elliptic curves E_n,E_(n theta), in Kummer coordinates(x+3ell,x-ell).
assertion.hypotheses: B has square reduced denominator,0<B<1/2 and v_p(B)>=4 for p in{2,3,5,7,13}; retain the split-cubic Kummer map, odd local formal-group calculation, local squareclass and reciprocity facts, CRT and Dirichlet.
assertion.quantifiers: For every such B choose m first, then beta,theta; construct one compatible auxiliary-prime assignment for both supports before selecting the actual primes.
assertion.parameter_range: beta>1,theta>=1 are coprime positive squarefree and prime to6; all auxiliary primes are distinct and avoid6 beta theta.
assertion.uniformity: The block determinant argument works for arbitrary d=omega(beta)>=1 and every finite theta support; no finite matrix test substitutes for it.
assertion.constants: The original2730 multiplier catalogue and old-prime valuation4 remain fixed; exactly d-1 I slots plus one q0 slot are used.
assertion.normalizations: Retain actual nonzero beta/theta cross-symbols and their two zero row sums; Ksharp=K+lambda a^t; q0 deletion and full-product determinant coefficient1. Selmer means full2-Selmer, not isogeny Selmer.
assertion.exceptional_cases: d=1 has empty I block; theta=1 permits identical two parameters. Necessary dyadic conditions give only an upper bound; the particular(beta,1) is separately checked locally at every place and independent of rational2-torsion.
assertion.limit_order: Reconcile all Legendre and local conditions before CRT/Dirichlet. Establish exact finite Selmer dimension before full-corank deduction or either use of RC; no rational point or finite Sha inferred here.

assertion.hypotheses: A is an elliptic curve over Q.
assertion.quantifiers: Every elliptic curve over Q; no semistability, residual-image or non-CM restriction.
assertion.parameter_range: Arithmetic conductor N of the same A, not an arbitrary enlarged level.
assertion.uniformity: Qualitative existence for each A; no effective degree bound.

assertion.exceptional_cases: C.16.4(b) Fricke formula excluded. No normalized newform, optimality, Manin constant or Hecke identity inferred.
assertion.limit_order: Choose A and its conductor, then its parametrization before forming later quotient maps.

assertion.limit_order: Reduce and augment where needed; retain actual maps and homotopies; take the inner limit; invert t and contract active blocks; obtain minimal ranks by unit cancellation.

assertion.statement: For the retained fixed-field common family, there are Delta,Q in O[G] with u_x=2^(-a) eta_x Q_x/Delta_x^3 wherever Delta_x!=0. With f=2^a Delta^4 and d=eta Delta Q, f_x u_x=d_x holds at every character, f0 lies in Lambda, v2 f0(0)<=c_det and the signwise negative Laurent cutoff is L_T(M)=16(d_K+5)M.
assertion.objects: The actual cycle z, closed integral functional mu=2^a lambda_z, corrected coordinate u, retained determinant unit kappa, original group ring O[G], and grouped central Smith disk blocks A_i with Delta=product det A_i.
assertion.hypotheses: The preceding fixed-field budget gives the retained finite free family and m<=d_K+5, central rank-one cohomology and integral new-local cancellation. The actual paired functional and correction eta are supplied by their separate constructions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every sign character, including those where Delta_x=0, and every positive precision M for the Laurent bound.
assertion.parameter_range: Fixed K and common family; O is the 2-adic completion of Lambda_(2), Lambda=Z2[[t]].
assertion.uniformity: The constants d_K,t_K,h_K are fixed after K and before the graph or binary dimension; a and c_E precede that choice.
assertion.constants: c_det=a+4(h_K+2c_E+2t_K); L_T(M)=16(d_K+5)M; denominator exponent3 and clearing power4 are fixed.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same actual z, functional, determinant basis and eta. Each grouped disk block is canceled once, and the inverse-determinant sign yields P=epsilon product_even delta_i^2.
assertion.exceptional_cases: When Delta_x=0 both f_x and d_x vanish, so no fraction with zero denominator is specialized. Acyclic constituents have the already defined zero coordinate. Only signwise Laurent support is bounded; no group-basis pole bound or bound for d is asserted.
assertion.limit_order: Cancel new local blocks retaining kappa; choose the constant central Smith bases; form original A_i determinants; cancel each grouped block once; then form Delta,Q,f,d in the original group ring before sign evaluation.

assertion.objects: The actual split derivative local model D0 plus(F plus S)[−1] plus D2[−2], its retained pairing, and the strict/relaxed/finite/singular Selmer cone complexes.
assertion.hypotheses: The old actual class spans generic H1 and localizes to nonzero v; its actual derivative has finite coordinate0 and singular coordinateJv. Retained integral local pairings/isotropy homotopies and exact global duality/localization identities are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: At each new inert derivative prime in the finite sequence, over the stated fraction or test field.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite and singular planes of rank2; localization v may be divisible in the integral lattice.
assertion.uniformity: The comparison preserves valuation at every allowed switch, without requiring a uniform divisibility bound on v.

assertion.limit_order: Retain the integral local model and triangles; pass to the specified test field; identify strict H1 and the relaxed annihilator; use the actual derivative; compare determinant lines with their common strict factor.

available_assertion.objects: Classical elliptic singular moduli of imaginary quadratic orders.
available_assertion.hypotheses: The elliptic curve has geometric complex multiplication by an imaginary quadratic order.

available_assertion.parameter_range: Negative order discriminants; elliptic curves in characteristic zero.
available_assertion.uniformity: Algebraic integrality for all such singular moduli.

available_assertion.normalizations: Use the classical elliptic Weierstrass c4^3/discriminant invariant and the full CM order, including nonmaximal orders.

available_assertion.limit_order: Fix the CM order and form its class polynomial.

assertion.statement: Restriction of the evaluated cohomology to the exact full-Tate/ring-class/quadratic kernel is injective on the characteristic-zero tests; residual H0 vanishing instead follows from moving inertia and does not assert residual irreducibility.
assertion.objects: Evaluated crossed homomorphisms, the exact kernel of sequences trivial on the full Tate and specified class/quadratic fields, and the fixed scalar z.
assertion.hypotheses: Retain the actual evaluated cocycle identities, fixed scalar acting by u^4 central modulo this kernel, u^4-1 nonzero, and the moving-inertia scalar difference t on the residual test.
assertion.quantifiers: Each permitted characteristic-zero inner test and the outer fraction-field test; residual assertion only for the stated scalar-inertia invariants.
assertion.parameter_range: Characteristic-zero coefficients where u^4-1 is invertible; residual coefficient field F2((t)) for the separate H0 assertion.
assertion.uniformity: Uses the one fixed scalar already constructed for the fixed elliptic curve; no new field-dependent exponent.
assertion.constants: The same nonzero scalar u^4-1 and residual unit t.
assertion.normalizations: z is central modulo the exact kernel, not itself an element of the kernel. A cocycle vanishing on the kernel satisfies (u^4-1)b(g)=(g-1)b(z).
assertion.exceptional_cases: No residual restriction-injectivity or rank-two localization is claimed; E[2] remains trivial rank2 and residual multiplicity is retained.
assertion.limit_order: Construct the fixed scalar and evaluated cocycle first, restrict to the exact kernel, invert u^4-1 only in characteristic zero; treat residual inertia separately.

Take the actual quotient from the previous card and the actual fixed curve, then choose the isogeny in the required direction. Discard the finite union of primes dividing 2N, both bad-reduction sets, and the finitely many excluded Shimura factors. At remaining primes compare reciprocal polynomial 1-a_q X+q X^2 with X=q^-s. Amir–Hong matches the traces; trivial character and dimension one match the determinants. Faltings is applied to A_f itself and E_l itself, not a twist, dual constituent, or abstract common coefficient field. The original base field is Q and the orientation is fixed by dual isogeny if necessary. The composite commutes with scalar multiplication. Only the comparison at almost all good finite primes is required. The documented erratum supplies eventual height stationarity, not constancy at every stage. The implication requires no finite Sha, BSD, conductor-by-conductor bad factor equality, or potential-isogeny descent. Use alpha q_f in the unchanged Pic0 composite and its good-Hecke intertwining, without any integral index or differential normalization claim.

assertion.statement: The actual primitive class-functional coordinate is regular at every height-one prime of Lambda other than(2), including(t) and(t+2), hence belongs to Lambda[1/2]. This regularity also holds at the unknown full-corank-one base.
assertion.objects: The actual primitive scalar Selmer complex, its actual class and own paired functional, and the integral derivative-switch complexes over each height-one DVR.
assertion.hypotheses: The starting generic kernel has rank one unless the actual class is zero; evaluation injection, characteristic-zero detection, exact local duality and actual-class determinant switch identities are supplied. Primitive integrality holds for the old local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every height-one prime different from(2), and each finite derivative list produced by the argument.
assertion.parameter_range: Known simple-zero ring instances and the unknown full-corank-one base, with the latter used only for regularity.
assertion.uniformity: No uniform numerical valuation bound at the unknown base is asserted. Finite switch termination is pointwise for the height-one test.
assertion.constants: All switch determinant factors are units; no new numerical constant or inverse localization value is introduced.
assertion.normalizations: At quadratic specialization the two signs are defined by actual conjugation, not a ring substitution. Finite and singular planes carry opposite J actions and exact symmetric hyperbolic cross pairing. Retain D0, strict torsion factors and the actual class-functional product.
assertion.exceptional_cases: At(t) and(t+2) use sign splitting and one-or-two-step descent, not nonquadratic irreducibility. Isotropy alone does not prove U=U-perp. Primitive vectors select primes but never replace the actual class. No inverse at an unused relaxed prime.
assertion.limit_order: Localize at a height-one prime; choose a primitive generic-kernel vector for detection; use actual derivative switches until dimension one; show the actual class and own functional integral there; transport unit-valued determinant comparisons back; intersect all height-one localizations.

assertion.exceptional_cases: Radicands need not be independent, no class number is divided out, and Tate and radical fields need not be disjoint.

assertion.statement: There is one integral universal correction eta in O[G] such that the same corrected relaxed coordinate tilde_u=eta*u_rel satisfies tilde_u_x=epsilon_x*u_prim,x at every character, with epsilon_x a Lambda unit. Central valuations and zeros transfer whenever the primitive coordinate is regular.
assertion.objects: Actual primitive-to-relaxed map i and paired strict map j, actual retained classes and their own closed functionals, unused-prime factors e_q=a_q-z-z^(-1), two-place quotient factor l_q, and finite binary groupG.
assertion.hypotheses: The retained norm identity and boundary, cup-pairing naturality and original integral determinant bases are supplied. Every graph prime, including unused ones, has the prescribed scalar exponent. Rational E[2] makes a_q even at good oddq.
assertion.quantifiers: Each unused good split prime and every character of the same finite binary family, with one eta before character evaluation.
assertion.parameter_range: Lambda=Z2[[t]], O its completed localization at(2); good oddq and common graph-wide moving character.
assertion.uniformity: The correction is constructed in the original O[G] for the whole family, without character-by-character interpolation or group-order denominators.
assertion.constants: l_q*u_rel=e_q^2*epsilon_q*u_prim; q^2*l_q=e_q^2+(q-1)(q-1-(z+z^(-1))*e_q); v_q=(l_q/e_q^2-1)/2.
assertion.normalizations: Both the actual class and its own paired functional contribute onee_q. Comparison signs and unit disks give Lambda units, not merelyO units. eta is the product of1+v_q(1+g_q).
assertion.exceptional_cases: eta_x can have a pole at t=0; only its product withu_rel,x is specialized. No integral self-duality of the primitive condition or interpolation ofepsilon_x is assumed.
assertion.limit_order: Use the actual norm boundary and pairing naturality; compare quotient determinants in retained bases; prove e_q is anO[G]unit via reduction t^2/(1+t); construct integralv_q and oneeta; then evaluate characters and transfer regular central data.

assertion.statement: For the retained global, primitive and derivative Selmer models, finite detecting evaluations give an H1 injection preserved by coefficient extension; their bounded outer quotient is a characteristic-zero DVR with uniformizer2, carrying the retained duality maps and approximate cycles as actual crossed homomorphisms.
assertion.objects: Actual retained cochain maps, product Galois groups, bounded finite detecting lists, primitive/derivative local conditions and O_infinity formed from valuation-bounded ring instances.
assertion.hypotheses: Fixed bounded minimal-model ranks, omega(k_j)≤A and a fixed number of derivative labels; retained evaluations and compatibility homotopies. Direct Selmer evaluation requires residual H0 isomorphism and H1 injection for the local conditions.
assertion.quantifiers: Every indicated coefficient extension and each sequence of the bounded ring instances; evaluation at arbitrary sequences of group elements.
assertion.parameter_range: Primitive and derivative models with the stated local conditions. Orthogonal zero/full models only after an actual contraction at the chosen test ring.
assertion.uniformity: Detecting lists have bounded length at most dimV+dimW, selected and padded before the common limit. No support-uniform rank beyond the stipulated bound.
assertion.constants: Uniformizer2; no quantitative rank bound is added beyond the retained (5.1) bound.
assertion.normalizations: O_infinity is the ultraproduct quotient by sequences whose 2-adic valuation tends to infinity. Cochain evaluation uses the same ultrafilter, full compatibility homotopies and integral minimal-model inverses.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No continuity claim on one original Galois group and no completeness claim for the outer DVR. Zero local conditions may contribute evaluation-invisible H1, so direct injection is not asserted there. Approximate cycles are not silently replaced by exact finite-stage cycles.
assertion.limit_order: Choose finite detecting lists and cone cancellations before the common inner limit; form the bounded outer quotient; pass actual matrices and homotopies; only then regard differential-tending-to-zero sequences as crossed homomorphisms.

assertion.objects: Conjugate transport c(z), the orthogonal comparison j, its retained homotopy inverse, and lambda_z=PD(-,j^(-1)c(z)) on bounded free inner-limit models.
assertion.hypotheses: The actual local Kummer diagrams, perfect coefficient pairing, orthogonal local conditions/isotropy homotopies and retained duality maps are supplied. Active/moving local complexes have the displayed integral contractions in their stated localizations. The fixed old local types and old class multiplier L are retained.
assertion.quantifiers: Every finite active list and binary groupG; every allowed K split at2N; every scalar primitive constituent and height-one prime p other than(2).
assertion.parameter_range: O is the2-adic completion of Z2[[t]] localized at(2). Assertions are after the inner limit, not inversions of t in finite Artin rings.
assertion.uniformity: One fixed old-support exponent independent ofG,the active list and allowedK; actual conventions permit a=0.
assertion.constants: a=0 is permitted because z already includesL; any larger fixed nonnegativea may be retained without dividingL or changingz.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same own functional ofz, not an arbitrary dual vector. Group algebra pairing is coefficient-of-identity ofab, with permutation matrix, not normalized trace divided by|G|.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Universal relaxed integrality overO[G] does not imply relaxed scalar integrality at every height-one prime. assertion.limit_order: Retain finite free diagrams and homotopies through inner limit; construct local contractions and fixed old-support comparisons; invertj in derived category and integrally on models; pair transportedz; only then compare generic values across localizations.

The unital Q-coefficient action is integer multiplication on integral scalars. Shimura's eigenrelation includes all its T_n. This card consumes its good-prime relation and its almost-all Euler comparison. Pulling back differentials along z to qz and (z+j)/q gives exactly q f(qz)+q^-1 sum_j f((z+j)/q). Moduli cyclic quotients and their duals exchange the two projections for q coprime to N. Use the same J0(N) and q_f on the degree-zero divisor classes, not a polarisation-dual map or a tangent-space substitute. No degree or averaging factor is inserted. A rationalized morphism equality descends to integral Hom by torsion-freeness. The good correspondence has q+1 branches at infinity, all fixing it. The rational cusp gives the Pic0 map and no extra constant. The Gamma0(N) branch makes the alternative Fricke condition unnecessary. No bad Euler, Atkin–Lehner, integral lattice or model extension conclusion is claimed. Postcompose with alpha and apply to [x]-[infinity]. The unaveraged CM and reduced neighbor relations consume this operator with their separate CM and reduction inputs.

assertion.statement: Each specified actual automorphism of the finite Galois compositum is realized by arithmetic Frobenius at a suitable chosen place over infinitely many rational primes, avoiding the finite exclusions.
assertion.objects: The finite normal composita containing the actual radical, cyclotomic, Tate, ring-class, quadratic and finite cochain data; a single automorphism whose restrictions already agree.
assertion.hypotheses: The extension is finite Galois over Q, the prescribed automorphism exists in its Galois group, and only finitely many primes are excluded.
assertion.quantifiers: For each such finite extension and actual automorphism, infinitely many unramified rational primes and a place over each realizing that representative.
assertion.parameter_range: Finite Galois extensions only; each precision is treated separately.
assertion.uniformity: No effective size bound, infinite-level density or uniformity over extension degree is asserted.
assertion.constants: The nonempty conjugacy class has positive density equal to its size divided by the finite Galois group order.
assertion.normalizations: Arithmetic Frobenius acts by the residue-field norm power. A rational prime determines a conjugacy class; conjugating the place selects the actual representative.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Compatibility on intersections is an input from an actual automorphism, not a consequence of Chebotarev. The theorem does not independently prescribe arbitrary component actions.
assertion.limit_order: Form the finite normal compositum and actual compatible element; apply finite Chebotarev and choose a place; only later pass to the retained precision limit or apply localized model maps.

original_use.reason: For the actual finite-rank group-ring coefficient, every finite quotient has finite H0. Thus its H0 images stabilize, giving Mittag-Leffler and zero lim1. The quotients by (2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1) and finite-group coefficient relations are cofinal with powers of the maximal ideal: the former quotient is finite local, hence has nilpotent maximal ideal; conversely its defining elements lie in any prescribed maximal-ideal power for sufficiently large a,n. Apply the source exact sequence to this cofinal system. The already proved norm compatibility supplies the compatible H1 elements; it is not supplied by this theorem. For K10 take R=Z_2[[Gamma]][G]=Z_2[[t]][G], where G is the fixed finite elementary abelian two-group, and take the free rank-two R-module T_2E tensor R with the actual continuous chi_0 psi kappa^(-1) action. R is a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m generated by2,t and g-1 for g in G; its residue field is F_2. The actual finite quotients use J_(a,n)=(2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1). The quotient R/J_(a,n) is finite and local: modulo2 it is the group algebra of the finite two-group Gamma_n times G, whose augmentation ideal is nilpotent. Hence some power of m is contained in J_(a,n). Conversely J_(a,n) is contained in any prescribed m^k for a,n sufficiently large: 2^a is in m^k for a>=k, while for 1<=i<k the coefficient binomial(2^n,i) has valuation at least n-v_2(i), and terms of degree i>=k are already in m^k. Thus these ideals and the m-adic powers define cofinal filtrations. Use a diagonal cofinal sequence in a,n. Each H0 of the finite quotient coefficient is a subgroup of a finite module, so its images stabilize and lim1 H0 vanishes. Apply Corollary4.1.3 to the complete finite-type admissible R-module through this cofinal identification. Norm compatibility of the already supplied classes produces their inverse-limit element; the argument proves no new norm relation.

Pairing two cocycles valued in the same minus eigenline gives zero by the alternating Weil pairing. The line is therefore isotropic and has half the dimension of this nondegenerate two-dimensional F2 space, hence is its own annihilator.

original_use.reason: The displayed two matrix products in the consumer give the dilation and normalized U_p² action. For c nonzero divisible by4, the character d -> (c/d) has conductor dividing |c|: write c=s²D with D the fundamental discriminant of its squareclass; the factor at2 is at most the 2-part of c. This includes c negative. Hence d-prime congruent d modulo c preserves that character, and d-prime congruent d modulo4 preserves epsilon. Since p does not divide d-prime, (p²/d-prime)=1. For V_p, multiplicativity gives (c/p /d)/(c/d)=(p/d). All square-root arguments are identically cz+d, so there is no branch comparison by squaring. If c=0, d=±1 and the same matrices give the triangular identity directly. The map r->(b+rd)/(a+rc) modulo p² is a bijection since a+rc is a unit and determinant is1. A finite set of rational translates has rational cusp images; after choosing a common cusp width, each expansion has nonnegative exponents, so the finite sum is holomorphic. Finally U_p² V_p=U_p coefficientwise. At each new p, p is prime to all previously fixed level factors, and this argument does not raise their exponents.

original_use.reason: For a unary generator F_lambda(tz), psi=lambda*chi_-4*(t/.). Choose a good p outside t and the character/sieve modulus. At n=t m² the first term is p lambda(p)a(n). If p does not divide m, the middle term is lambda(p)a(n), because chi_-4(p)*(t/p)*(-t/p)=1, and the last term is zero. If p divides m, the middle term is zero and the last term is lambda(p)a(n), including zero coefficients of the imprimitive character. At indices outside t times a square all three terms vanish. Thus the eigenvalue is lambda(p)(p+1), of absolute value p+1. The standard unary space is spanned by such generators: a one-variable lattice/coset theta has a periodic odd coefficient after clearing denominators; partition its finite residue set by gcd strata and expand each function on the remaining unit group in Dirichlet characters. Oddness retains only odd characters, and a gcd factor becomes a square dilation. For any fixed finite collection these presentations have a common finite bad set. Only one prime outside it is needed below.

original_use.reason: Factor both Dirichlet characters through the Galois group of a common cyclotomic extension. For each element choose a good prime with that Frobenius using finite-abelian density. The already established equality at that prime gives equality on the chosen element. This proves character equality without using the conditional Euler formula or semisimple representation theory.
